newsitem.title: GERMANY: Controversial Bonn diplomat comes full circle.
newsitem.headline: Controversial Bonn diplomat comes full circle.

text.p: A German former diplomat who caused a storm by accepting a lucrative industrial post after retiring early on health grounds is set to complete a remarkable full circle when he returns to the foreign ministry this month.
Ministry sources said on Thursday Juergen Sudhoff, a former ambassador to Paris, would run the political department responsible for Asia, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America.

Sudhoff's return to the ministry looks like something of a miraculous recovery for a man who was medically declared "permanently unfit to serve" just last year. The nature of his health problems was never revealed.

He then took up an offer to work for Daimler-Benz AG, whipping up a storm among politicians and leading newspapers who questioned how he could be fit enough to work for Germany's biggest company but not for the foreign ministry.

Sudhoff responded by saying his new job as Daimler's Paris representative was confined to normal office hours and much less strenuous than his days as an ambassador when he worked from 6.30 a.m. until midnight.

The affair seemed to have been finally cleared up in September last year when Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel banned Sudhoff from taking the job on the grounds that it would "damage the interests of the service".

But Sudhoff has since produced a new medical certificate to say he is fit again and, under rules for public servants, the ministry has no option but to take him back and offer him a job with similar status and salary to his last one.

"An extraordinary series of events in the German foreign service has now reached its extraordinary conclusion," the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung daily newspaper commented in a report on the case on Thursday.
